verdict.rationale: Amazon SES has a documented public API. Its v2 API reference covers the SendEmail operation with Simple, Raw and Templated message types, and the docs say users can call the SES API directly or through AWS SDKs. Probes also confirm machine-readable docs: llms.txt and markdown versions of the doc pages both return HTTP 200. Missing for 10: no OpenAPI/Swagger spec was found at the probed paths, and there is no independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven API use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: you can send email from Amazon EC2 by using an AWS SDK, by using the Amazon SES SMTP interface, or by making calls directly to the Amazon SES API
You can use the Amazon SES API v2 to send the following types of messages: Simple ... Raw ... Templated
